articles.title: US tells European countries to not 'poke' Russia as Putin says 'ready for war'
articles.summary: The US has urged several NATO allies, including Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, to tone down their public warnings about the threat posed by Russia,
articles.body: The US has urged several NATO allies, including Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, to tone down their public warnings about the threat posed by Russia, cautioning European countries against rhetoric that could further strain relations with Moscow, according to a Reuters report.The messages, delivered by Pentagon officials during bilateral meetings in recent weeks, reflect the Trump administration's concern that some European leaders' statements about Russia could undermine continental security. Four people familiar with the discussions told Reuters that Washington had advised its allies to avoid publicly portraying Moscow as increasingly desperate or cornered as its invasion of Ukraine slows.Among the US officials conveying the message was Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby, who is also involved in an ongoing review of American troop levels in Europe. The Pentagon declined to comment on the reported exchanges. "Private conversations among allies are just that, so we will not comment on these allegations," a Pentagon official told Reuters.Colby told a Baltic official recently that there should be no "poking" directed at the Russians, Reuters reported.Russian President Vladimir Putin has issued another warning to Europe, declaring that Moscow is prepared for a potential conflict even though it does not want a war."We are ready, but we want no war with Europe," Putin said, adding that countries seeking a confrontation should prepare for one. "And if things go too far, there will be no winners at all. Let no one forget that."As reported by The Independent, Putin's remarks followed a phone conversation with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere on Tuesday. The two leaders had sought to influence Moscow's position on the Ukraine conflict, stressing the importance of de-escalation and expressing continued support for Kyiv.Their decision to speak directly with Putin, however, drew criticism from other European leaders, who called for unity in dealing with Russia.Putin also warned against restrictions on navigation in the Baltic Sea, saying Moscow would respond to any challenge. articles.title: Toronto real estate CEO and two daughters shot during home invasion, wife attacked with hammer
articles.summary: A shocking early morning home invasion in Toronto's Bridle Path neighborhood left a prominent real estate CEO and his daughters injured after they were shot by masked intruders. The incident raises concerns about safety in affluent areas.
articles.body: A 75-year-old Canadian real estate CEO and his two daughters were shot after three masked men broke into their family home in an affluent Toronto neighbourhood early Thursday morning. His wife was also struck with a hammer during the attack.David Morton, head of Toronto-based MAC Group, and his family were inside their gated property in the Bridle Path neighbourhood when the intruders entered the five-bedroom residence at around 3.45am, The Toronto Sun reported.The suspects, who were carrying handguns and a hammer, reportedly gained access through a back door. Morton and his daughters, Maggie Zohil-Morton and Cristina Zohil-Morton, confronted the men inside the house, leading to a struggle." A struggle ensued during this altercation in which the suspects fired their guns multiple times and one victim was struck with a hammer," Toronto Police Service Inspector Kristy Smith told reporters.Morton and one of his daughters suffered gunshot wounds to their legs, while the other daughter was shot under her arm, according to the newspaper. Morton's wife, Doriana Zohil-Morton, who is also president of MAC Group, was struck with a hammer by one of the intruders.Smith said two family members suffered "life-altering injuries" and remained in hospital, while the other two sustained injuries that were not considered life-threatening. Police did not identify the victims based on their individual injuries.The three suspects fled the property in an SUV. Police have not released their descriptions or confirmed whether anything was taken from the residence.Investigators are examining a possible robbery motive. Smith said the intruders made demands for valuables during the confrontation, although it remains unclear whether they managed to take anything."There was a violent interaction. There was a demand made for valuables from within the home. Whether or not they escaped with anything is uncertain at this point," she said.Smith added that the suspects may have targeted the neighbourhood because of the wealth of its residents."An affluent area where people would have things that are sought after would be the motivation for this," she said.The Bridle Path is known for its large properties and luxury homes. An online listing for the family's residence describes a property with more than five bedrooms, seven bathrooms, a tennis court, an in-ground swimming pool and private gardens.Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow condemned the attack and called on residents to share any information that could help investigators."I am deeply troubled by the violent home invasion early this morning in the Bridle Path neighbourhood. My thoughts are with the family and their loved ones, who are going through something no family should ever have to face. I am praying for their full recovery," Chow wrote on XMorton leads MAC Group, a family-owned Toronto business with divisions covering real estate, hospitality and corporate housing. According to the company's website, he has around 30 years of experience in the hospitality and real estate industries.His daughter Cristina is listed as the founder of Zohil-Morton Law, which provides Canadian immigration law services. articles.title: Indian-origin woman who went missing in August found dead in a canal in California. Detectives had looked into the canal before but could not locate her
articles.summary: 72-year-old Ajit Kaur, an Indian-origin woman who was reported missing in August, was found dead in a California canal.
articles.body: 72-year-old Ajit Kaur, an Indian-origin woman who was reported missing in August, was found dead in a California canal. Kaur's body was found by a Turlock Irrigation District employee in the Lower Lateral 3 Canal near Central Avenue and Keyes Road in Ceres, California, on Saturday, October 24, CPD said. The employee had been conducting one of the district’s multiple daily patrols of the canal system at the time.Officers responded to the scene and confirmed that the remains were human. The remains were sent to the Stanislaus County Coroner's Office, where they identified the body on Tuesday.The area where Kaur's remains were found was examined by the detectives earlier. Kaur was reported missing from the Casa Grande Apartment complex in Ceres on August 23. She was last seen that day, at approximately 1:45 a.m. near Whitmore Ave and Mitchell Road in Ceres. Detectives said their investigation led them to believe that Kaur “may have entered” the TID canal located east of the apartment complex. CPD said they “pursued available leads and conducted extensive efforts to locate” her.This included canvassing the “surrounding area,” including canal areas throughout Ceres and working with a K9 with the Merced County Sheriff’s Office trained to track and locate missing persons.The Stanislaus County Sheriff’s Department Dive Unit also assisted in the search, deploying an underwater remote sonar drone to scan the canals. Detectives worked with TID to map potential water routes she may have taken and investigate whether she could have reached the TID regulating reservoir.“The Ceres Police Department extends its heartfelt condolences to Kaur’s family and loved ones during this difficult time,” CPD said in a statement. “Our thoughts are with them as they navigate this loss.” “We are grateful to the agencies and personnel who assisted throughout this investigation,” they added.When Kaur disappeared, the family members said that she was on her daily walk and then never returned. “No phone, no IDs, nothing whatsoever,” said Kaur’s daughter-in-law, Raman Atwal. “That’s very unusual for her.” They said Kaur was visually impaired in one eye and did not have any access to vehicle. articles.title: Dolly Parton’s father could not read or write; his struggle inspired her free book programme, which began in one Tennessee county and has now gifted over 330 million books worldwide
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's contribution to children's literacy began with a family story.
articles.body: Dolly Parton's contribution to children's literacy began with a family story. Growing up in rural Tennessee, the singer watched her father work hard to support his family, despite having had little opportunity for formal education. He never learnt to read or write, something Parton later believed had limited the opportunities available to him. Years afterwards, that experience became the starting point for a charitable project that would reach children far beyond the Appalachian community where she was raised. Reportedly, through the Dollywood Foundation's Imagination Library, Parton helped establish a programme that sends free books to young children, building a legacy measured in millions of deliveries.How Dolly Parton's father inspired her Imagination Library literacy missionParton grew up in Sevier County, Tennessee, in a large family with limited financial resources. Her father, Robert Lee Parton, worked as a farmer and construction worker. As reported by Fortune, Parton said during her Carnegie Medal acceptance speech, “This actually started because my father could not read and write, and I saw how crippling that could be”.“My dad was a very smart man. And I often wondered what he could have done had he been able to read and write. So that is the inspiration.”Parton later acknowledged that her father's inability to read may have prevented him from pursuing some of the ambitions he had during his life. She also spoke about how literacy could affect a person's independence, access to opportunities and confidence in everyday situations.The experience eventually gave her an idea for a charitable initiative. Rather than limiting her support to financial donations or individual educational projects, she wanted to make books available to children before they reached school age. Her father became the inspiration behind the plan, which she regarded as a tribute to him.Dolly Parton's Imagination Library first launched in 1995 through the Dollywood Foundation. Its first programme operated in Sevier County, the same part of Tennessee where she had spent her childhood.How the Imagination Library began reaching childrenAs reported by Fortune, Children in the participating area could receive a free book every month from birth until their first year of school. Parents did not have to purchase the titles or meet household income requirements to participate where the programme operated.The initiative depended on partnerships with local organisations, which helped cover distribution costs and organise registration. This arrangement allowed the programme to move beyond its original location without requiring the foundation to manage every local operation independently.The BBC reported, its expansion began in the United States in 2000. Canada joined in 2006, followed by the United Kingdom in 2007. Australia became part of the programme in 2013, while Ireland followed in 2019.The monthly deliveries were intended to make books a familiar part of childhood rather than something introduced only when formal education began. Families could build reading into everyday routines, with children receiving new titles as they grew.Reportedly, by the programme's 30th anniversary in 2025, more than 300 million books had been distributed. The organisation subsequently reported that the total had passed 330 million, reflecting the scale the initiative had reached since its beginnings in a single Tennessee county.Free books became part of family routinesFor many households, the programme's influence extended beyond the arrival of a parcel in the post. Parents described how receiving a new book each month encouraged them to establish regular reading habits with their children.London mother Harriet Anscombe, for example, registered her daughter when she was just three months old. The books became part of the family's bedtime routine, giving them a regular opportunity to read together. Anscombe said the early introduction to storybooks meant reading had become an established activity long before her daughter reached nursery or school age.According to the BBC reports, in Colorado, another family found that the programme helped create lasting memories around particular titles. Ciara Fernandez Faber's son developed an attachment to I Am A Rainbow, a children's book written by Parton.The book also gave the child a familiar connection to its author. When Parton's photograph appeared in the book, he referred to her as the 'Book Queen'.The programme reached children with different learning needsThe benefits reported by participating families have varied, depending on the ages and circumstances of their children. In Australia, mother Paige Stewart noticed changes in her twin daughters after they began receiving the monthly books. The girls had experienced speech delays and learning difficulties, and Stewart recalled that a book about colours helped them recognise and begin saying the names of different colours. As reported, she particularly remembered one of the girls saying 'orange', a word that delighted the family. The books subsequently became part of their efforts to encourage speech and communication.In Ireland, mother Helen Cashell signed up both her children. She appreciated the range of subjects covered in the selected titles, including different family structures, bullying, courage and identity. The books gave her children an introduction to experiences and people they might not otherwise encounter in their immediate surroundings.The selection process has also provided opportunities for children's authors. British writer Selina Brown, whose book My Rice Is Best was chosen for the programme, said around 14,000 copies of her title were distributed to children in the UK. The story features a Black protagonist, giving young readers access to a wider range of characters and experiences.A growing charitable legacy beyond the United StatesAlthough Parton remained the face of the initiative, its international expansion relied on local organisations and community partners who helped distribute books. Parents, grandparents and caregivers also encouraged families to register, sometimes introducing the scheme through newborn gifts.In Alabama, grandmother Kristina Hadley registered her granddaughter before she was born. The child now has a dedicated bookshelf for her monthly deliveries, and Hadley regularly recommends the programme to other families.What began in Parton's home county has since become an international literacy initiative, reaching millions of children with free books and encouraging families to read together.Her father's memory remains at the centre of the initiativeParton often spoke about the personal importance of the Imagination Library. In an open letter published on the programme's website, she explained that her father had been one of the people who influenced her most, despite never having had the opportunity to develop basic literacy skills.The Dollywood Foundation's work has since reached far beyond the original community in Tennessee. More than 300 million books have been distributed, with children in several countries receiving a new title each month through local partnerships.For Parton, the idea had started with the educational opportunities her father missed. The programme that followed turned that family experience into a long-running literacy effort, allowing millions of children to begin building their own collections of books before starting school.You use AI every day. articles.title: An 18-year-old Mississippi woman who relied on family for rides to work was blindfolded by a family friend and surprised with a free car after a local repair business stepped in to help
articles.summary: An 18-year-old woman in Biloxi, Mississippi, was blindfolded before being surprised with a car she could use to get to work.
articles.body: An 18-year-old woman in Biloxi, Mississippi, was blindfolded before being surprised with a car she could use to get to work. A family friend who knew about her circumstances contacted Classic Collision for help. The collision repair business had previously given cars to people in need. Rylee Brown was taken to the location blindfolded and asked to trust the people guiding her. When she removed the blindfold, she found a vehicle waiting for her there. The surprise took place on Monday, February 16, and left Brown expressing excitement and gratitude as she received the car. According to WLOX, the gift was arranged through the efforts of a family friend and the collision repair business.How a family friend helped arrange the surpriseLara Alley, a family friend, knew Brown long before the surprise was arranged. She said, “I’ve known Rylee since before she was born. Her mom was one of my best friends. We were next-door neighbors for about 40 years.”After learning about Brown’s circumstances, Alley reached out to Classic Collision for help. The company had previously provided cars to people in need. Her outreach brought Brown’s situation to Classic Collision, whose regional director, James Steed, said, “When you get that call that touches your heart, you jump in and you help.”No further details were provided about how Alley and the business arranged the vehicle or how long the preparations took before Brown was brought to the location.How does the company respond to requests for helpJames Steed explained that the company steps in to help when it hears about someone’s circumstances. Classic Collision had given cars to people in need before Brown’s case. The vehicle’s model, age and value were not disclosed. It was also unclear whether the car had been donated by the business, one of its employees or another individual.Classic Collision was described as a local collision repair business, but no details were given about a formal programme behind its previous vehicle donations. Steed’s comments focused on the company’s willingness to step in when people asked for help.A blindfolded arrival ends with an unexpected giftBrown later recalled the moment she was led into the location blindfolded and surprised with the car.She said, “Basically, I just got brought here blindfolded, and then, they were like, ‘Here, just trust me. Walk with me.’ Then, all of a sudden, they are like, ‘Take it off,’ and BAM! There’s a car, and I’m like ‘What!’ I was kind of hoping for a car, and I’m so glad I got a car because I need one.”Her comments also reflected the practical importance of the gift as she had depended on family members for transport, including trips to and from work.How did Steed respond to Brown’s excitementBrown drove away in her new car with her father sitting beside her in the passenger seat.Steed said he was pleased by her response after receiving the car. articles.title: Two days of rain bring Delhi’s AQI down to 60; minister credits ‘targeted action’ for cleaner air
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: After two days of rainfall brought considerable relief from pollution in the national capital, Delhi minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Friday
articles.body: NEW DELHI: After two days of rainfall brought considerable relief from pollution in the national capital, Delhi minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Friday credited the government’s “targeted action” and public participation for the improvement in air quality, even as a report pointed to the significant role played by favourable weather conditions.Sirsa shared visuals of India Gate on X, highlighting an AQI reading of 93 and describing it as “Satisfactory”. He said the improvement showed that targeted action was producing results."Seeing visuals of India Gate with a 'Satisfactory' AQI of 93 is proof that targeted action brings real results. Under the leadership of CM Rekha Gupta, our government is working round the clock on anti-pollution measures, but real change happens when governance is backed by strong Jan Bhagidari. A huge thank you to the people of Delhi for their active participation in our mission for clean air. Let’s keep working together for a healthier, greener Delhi!!" Sirsa posted on X.However, Delhi's air quality improvement has coincided with an unusually wet October.As per news agency PTI, the city recorded an average AQI of 167 this month, its lowest October average since 2015, according to an analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).The AQI stood at 60 on Friday, making it the cleanest October day since October 10, 2022, when it was recorded at 44. The highest AQI recorded this month was 245, the lowest monthly peak since 2015.As per the PTI report, Delhi received 61.4mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending 8.30am on Friday, making it the wettest October day in four years and the sixth wettest October day since 1951. The city recorded cumulative rainfall of 123.3mm till 8.30am on Friday, more than eight times its monthly normal of 15.1mm.The improvement in air quality comes against the backdrop of a series of unusually wet days. The city recorded five days of 'poor' air quality, three 'satisfactory' days and 22 'moderate' days in October so far. Air quality entered the 'poor' category on October 21, when the AQI rose to 245.Manoj Kumar of CREA pointed to the influence of weather conditions while assessing the improvement in pollution levels."Delhi recorded a relatively lower average AQI in October 2026 compared with previous Octobers, although it remained 1.5 times higher than the average AQI for September 2026."AQI was already relatively low before GRAP (Graded Response Action Plan) was imposed, and declined to 60 on October 30, coinciding with 61.4 mm of rainfall at Safdarjung. This highlights the importance of accounting for meteorological influences before attributing improvements in air quality to GRAP measures."Delhi's average AQI in October was 167 this year, compared with 223 in 2025, 234 in 2024, 219 in 2023, 210 in 2022 and 264 in 2015. Its average AQI between January and October stood at 168, the lowest for the period since 2020, when it was 156.The capital also recorded its wettest October in four years, with 123.3 mm of rainfall till Friday morning. It was also the coldest October day in terms of maximum temperature since 1951, with the maximum temperature at Safdarjung settling at 20.7 degrees Celsius on Friday.The data highlights the role of rainfall and other meteorological conditions in the recent improvement in Delhi's air quality, even as the government continues to highlight its anti-pollution measures.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.summary: A striking silver cabin shaped like an airship has become one of Scotland’s most recognisable holiday rentals, and now the business behind it is on the
articles.body: A striking silver cabin shaped like an airship has become one of Scotland’s most recognisable holiday rentals, and now the business behind it is on the market. AirShip 002, along with two neighbouring retreats at Druim Na Cracaig on the Morvern Peninsula near Oban, has been listed by Savills for offers over £750,000. The collection of architecturally designed properties generates around £100,000 in gross annual income and has attracted guests from around the world, including visitors from Japan. The sale offers more than a distinctive place to stay. It includes a proven hospitality business, a four-acre elevated coastal site, and three properties that have become destinations in their own right. According to The Scotsman, AirShip 002 has earned international attention for its curved aluminium form, dragonfly windows, and dramatic views over the Sound of Mull, while the wider portfolio has appeared on television programs and regularly features in lists of Britain’s most unusual holiday homes. Read more details about it here:The cabin that looks like an AirshipAirShip 002 was designed by architect Roderick James and designer Amanda Markham as a modern interpretation of a streamlined airship. Its aluminium-clad exterior, curved silhouette, and distinctive dragonfly windows give it the appearance of a futuristic vessel resting above the Scottish coastline. The cabin sits in a remote setting with panoramic sea views toward the Ardnamurchan Peninsula and across the Sound of Mull.The unusual design has made AirShip 002 one of the most wish-listed Airbnb properties in the United Kingdom. Savills describes it as an internationally recognised retreat with a large collection of five-star guest reviews and a loyal following. Its appeal lies not only in its appearance, but in the sense of escape it offers: a compact, carefully designed cabin set within one of Scotland’s most dramatic coastal landscapes.The cabin’s success inspired the creation of two additional retreats. The PilotHouse is a two-storey hideaway with an elliptical form and a raised first floor living space designed to maximize views toward Tobermory and the open sea. The Captain’s Cabin is a smaller, nautically inspired escape with a private rooftop viewing balcony, a cosy salon, a pantry kitchen, a double bedroom, and a shower room.A business with a proven incomeThe Druim Na Cracaig portfolio is being sold as an established holiday rental business rather than simply a collection of unusual buildings. articles.title: A UK woman claimed she could not walk, drive or work because of hip pain, but investigators found she was running a body-piercing business and working for other clients
articles.summary: A UK woman who claimed that hip pain left her unable to walk, drive or work has been ordered to pay more than £6,000 after admitting to fraudulently
articles.body: A UK woman who claimed that hip pain left her unable to walk, drive or work has been ordered to pay more than £6,000 after admitting to fraudulently claiming Statutory Sick Pay while working for other clients and running her own body-piercing business. Claire Hopkinson, a resident of Telford, Shropshire, submitted false medical fitness certificates, WhatsApp messages and emails to support her claims that she could not perform her duties as a personal carer. However, an investigation by Telford & Wrekin Council uncovered evidence that she was working as a personal assistant for two other individuals through a private care company. Investigators also found that she had fabricated claims about hospital stays and undergoing a hip replacement operation. She pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation on December 1, 2025.How the sick pay fraud was uncoveredAccording to Telford & Wrekin Council, Hopkinson fraudulently claimed Statutory Sick Pay between March 28, 2024, and October 28, 2024, while employed as a privately employed personal carer.During this period, she submitted medical fitness certificates, commonly known as fit notes, alongside WhatsApp messages and emails claiming that hip pain prevented her from working.She alleged that she could not walk, drive or perform her duties as a personal assistant. However, investigators discovered that she was working for two other individuals through a private care company while also operating her own local body-piercing business.The investigation also uncovered false claims about hospital stays and a hip replacement operation. The council said the medical events she described had been fabricated.Hopkinson received £3,261.65 in Statutory Sick Pay to which she was not entitled, according to the council's investigation.She fabricated hospital stays and a hip replacement operationThe investigation found that Hopkinson had gone beyond claiming that she was unable to work because of hip pain.According to the council, she fabricated accounts of hospital stays and claimed to have undergone a hip replacement operation. These claims were found to be false during the investigation.Her medical fitness certificates and electronic communications formed part of the evidence examined by investigators.The case ultimately led to her admitting to fraud by false representation. The council said the court highlighted the seriousness of the offence, including the extent of her attempts to cover up her actions.The authority has not published further details about the medical documents, the precise investigative methods used or how the false claims were independently verified.How much money did she have to pay?Hopkinson received £3,261.65 in Statutory Sick Pay through the fraudulent claims. Following her guilty plea, the court ordered her to pay a fine and costs totalling £2,814.She was also required to repay the falsely claimed sick pay directly to Telford & Wrekin Council.The combined amount exceeds £6,000, according to the authority.The financial consequences therefore include both the repayment of the money she received and the additional fine and court costs. The council's announcement does not confirm whether the full amount has already been repaid.She pleaded guilty to fraud by false representationHopkinson was interviewed under caution by council officers during the investigation and eventually admitted to the deception.On December 1, 2025, she pleaded guilty to fraud by false representation at court.The case was subsequently publicised by Telford & Wrekin Council on December 16, 2025, as part of its efforts to highlight action against fraud involving public funds.The council did not report a prison sentence in its announcement. Instead, it detailed the financial orders imposed following her guilty plea and confirmed that she was repaying the sick pay directly to the authority.Council says fraud diverts resources from those who need supportCouncillor Richard Overton, deputy leader of Telford & Wrekin Council and cabinet member for highways, housing and enforcement, said the case demonstrated the authority's commitment to tackling fraud and protecting public funds.He said fraudulent claims undermine trust and divert resources away from people who genuinely need support.The council also encouraged residents to report suspected fraud so that public money could be safeguarded and used to support those who need it.Hopkinson's case formed part of the authority's wider enforcement efforts to investigate suspected fraud and pursue action where wrongdoing is established.What is Statutory Sick Pay in the UK?Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is a payment available to eligible employees who are unable to work because of illness. It is distinct from disability benefits and other forms of financial assistance.In Hopkinson's case, the fraud involved claiming SSP while allegedly being unable to work as a personal carer, despite undertaking other paid work and operating a business.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kate Winslet reads ‘Room on the Broom’ for children during the Halloween season, adding its 104th read-aloud to Storyline Online’s free literacy library
articles.summary: “The witch had a cat, and a hat that was black...” Kate Winslet’s voice rises and falls with the rhythm, turning each line into a visual as she reads
articles.body: “The witch had a cat, and a hat that was black...” Kate Winslet’s voice rises and falls with the rhythm, turning each line into a visual as she reads Julia Donaldson’s ‘Room on the Broom’. She does not rush. Rather, she lets the beat carry the story. The Academy Award-winning actor reads Room on the Broom in the latest video from Storyline Online, the children’s literacy programme that is free to watch at any hour. The read-aloud went live earlier this month on StorylineOnline.net and on the programme’s YouTube channel, just as the Halloween season gets underway.‘Room on the Broom’Written by Julia Donaldson and illustrated by Axel Scheffler, ‘Room on the Broom’ follows a friendly witch and her cat as they fly through the sky. When the wind blows away the witch’s hat, broom and wand, a helpful dog, bird and frog retrieve her belongings. In return, each of them asks for just one thing: a ride on the broom. The witch agrees and makes room for each new friend. However, the broom cannot hold the growing group of passengers and eventually snaps in two. The passengers tumble to the ground. When the witch suddenly finds herself face-to-face with a hungry dragon, her new friends must work together to come to her rescue.The story is filled with adventure and laced with humour. ‘Room on the Broom’ celebrates kindness, inclusion and the power of friendship. Julia Donaldson’s playful rhymes add to the beauty of the story.Kate Winslet knows the bookWinslet knows the book well. She has read it to all her children. The fun, adventure and warmth that Winslet’s voice brings to the story are not entirely accidental. “I have read this book to all of my children, and it’s from the same author as ‘The Gruffalo’ and the same illustrator as ‘The Gruffalo’, and the same author and illustrator, too, as ‘The Smartest Giant in Town’. I really love being able to go into the worlds of these authors because they are imaginative. They are fun. There are always lots of characters. And as a person who loves reading stories to children, there are always lots of fun and silly voices to do,” Winslet said in a statement. Her performance leans into those voices, giving each animal its own personality as the witch’s journey gets busier and noisier. All these elements also make the book a perfect fit for the Halloween season.The SAG-AFTRA Foundation sees the book’s staying power as part of its appeal. Courtney B. Vance, President and Chairman of the Foundation, pointed to the lasting message beneath the spells and flying: “Room on the Broom has delighted children and families for 25 years because beneath all of the magic and adventure is a beautiful message about kindness, generosity and making room for others. Kate is an extraordinary storyteller, and we are thrilled to have her bring this beloved book to life for Storyline Online. It’s the perfect story to share with children, families and classrooms as we head into the Halloween season.”Storyline Online is produced by the nonprofit SAG-AFTRA Foundation and draws millions of views each month. Winslet’s reading is the 104th read-aloud in the library, which already includes performances by Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Viola Davis, Oprah Winfrey and Michelle Yeoh, among many others. Each video pairs an actor’s reading with illustrations created for the programme. Families and teachers can watch the video for free at StorylineOnline.net, where the full library is also available. The video also comes with a free activity guide aligned with Common Core Standards, designed to encourage reading comprehension and creative play in the classroom or at home.You use AI every day. articles.title: 3 held for wildlife hunting in Jaisalmer
articles.summary: Forest Department arrests 3 for alleged fox and rabbit hunting near Swangiya Mata Temple in Jaisalmer; animals died; case filed under Wildlife Act.
articles.body: Jaisalmer: The Forest Department has arrested three men for allegedly hunting wild animals, including a fox and a rabbit, near Swangiya Mata Temple in Gajroopsagar area of Kishanghat in Jaisalmer. Both animals were found in a semi-conscious condition and later died despite medical treatment.Three accused were arrested late Thursday evening after a tip-off about illegal hunting near a temple. A Forest Department team raided and cordoned off the area before apprehending them.On Friday, they were produced before a court, which remanded them to judicial custody.Jaisalmer Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Kumar Shubham said the department had received specific information that some people were hunting rare wildlife in Gajroopsagar area near Swangiya Mata Temple.Acting on the information, a team from the Jaisalmer Forest Range, under the supervision of Regional Forest Officer Shyam Sunder Nagora and Assistant Conservator of Forests Dilip Singh Rathore, raided the location and caught the suspects.The accused have been identified as Mularam, Uttamaram and Chandranath, all residents of Jaisalmer district.During the operation, the forest officials recovered a fox and a rabbit in a semi-conscious condition from their possession. Fox is listed under Schedule I and rabbit under the relevant protected schedule of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended in 2022.Considering their critical condition, the animals were immediately shifted to a veterinary hospital for treatment. A medical team from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) was also called in to assist in their rescue and treatment. However, despite the efforts of the veterinary experts, both animals succumbed to their injuries and died during treatment.The Forest Department also seized a traditional wildlife trapping device known as 'Kud', other equipment allegedly used for hunting, and two motorcycles from the accused. A case has been registered against them under the relevant provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and they were questioned in detail.DFO Kumar Shubham said illegal hunting and wildlife crimes pose a serious threat to biodiversity and ecological balance. articles.title: EU and Canada seek deeper ties amid worsening global uncertainty
articles.summary: Both sides signed a digital trade deal, as Trump’s trade threats push Washington’s allies to seek closer ties elsewhere.
articles.body:
The European Union and Canada have launched what they described as an Alliance for the Future, as Ottawa prepares to become the bloc’s first so-called “associate member” .

Prime Minister Mark Carney hosted the Canada-EU summit in Montreal and signed a digital trade deal, alongside other agreements. Also at the Friday summit were European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa.

The term “associate member” has no legal basis and is contested by some EU states. However, its use underscores the desire of Canada and the EU to forge closer relations, as United States President Donald Trump continues to threaten Washington’s traditional allies with trade tariffs if they do not play by his rules.

“Canada and the EU are working to establish the closest possible partnership, which will be far from full membership, but which will make Canada the first associate member of the European Union,” Carney posted on X.

“Today in Montreal, we have taken a major step forward by establishing more than twenty measures that will increase affordability, create opportunities and ensure our sovereignty on both sides of the Atlantic.”

In a joint statement following the summit, the two sides announced an agreement under which the European Investment Bank will invest in critical Canadian resources, particularly raw minerals. They also said they would advance cooperation on artificial intelligence security and safety.

“A more dangerous and divided world has fundamentally changed the requirements of sovereignty. It is no longer enough for nations to feed, fuel and defend ourselves,” the statement said.

It added that “true sovereignty” requires secure access to critical minerals, semiconductors, payment systems, energy, vaccines, space-based communications and AI.

Ukraine was also on the meeting agenda, with Carney announcing Canada’s participation in the EU’s 90 billion euro ($103bn) support loan for Kyiv. Carney said Canada would make an initial contribution of 500 million euros ($558m).

Opportunities for students in Canada and the EU were also discussed. Both sides said they would launch negotiations aimed at deepening Ottawa’s participation in Erasmus+, the EU’s flagship student exchange programme.

Carney and Trump are currently engaged in a trade dispute, with talks under way to reach a deal between the two countries.

articles.title: A retired Virginia optometrist opened an ice-cream shop in 2021 to create jobs for people with disabilities; her two stores now employ 35 and she says there is a waiting list to work there
articles.summary: By 2026, Robin Rinearson’s two Fairfax County businesses have become more than neighbourhood food shops, they have become workplaces where people with
articles.body: By 2026, Robin Rinearson’s two Fairfax County businesses have become more than neighbourhood food shops, they have become workplaces where people with disabilities can build skills, confidence and independence. When retired optometrist Robin Rinearson opened Jake’s Ice Cream in Virginia in 2021, her goal was not simply to sell scoops of ice cream. She wanted to create something she felt was missing: meaningful, long-term employment opportunities for people with disabilities. Five years later, that small idea has grown into two businesses employing 35 people, 24 at Jake’s Ice Cream and 11 at Jake’s Gourmet Popcorn. Rinearson now says she has a waiting list of people hoping to work there. The story was reported by local news outlet FFXnow after Fairfax County supervisors recognised Rinearson on August 25 for her inclusive hiring practices. Earlier this summer, the Professional Baseball Athletic Trainers Society (PBATS) also named her a 2026 Ability Transcends Challenges Award recipient.It began with her nephewThe ice-cream shop was named after Rinearson’s nephew, Jake, who has cerebral palsy. Before the pandemic, Jake had held a job for years. But when Covid-19 disrupted workplaces, Rinearson became increasingly concerned about how easily people with disabilities could be pushed out of employment when adequate accommodations were not available. That experience helped shape her decision to open Jake’s Ice Cream in August 2021.Earlier reporting by Patch found that the shop initially employed 11 people, many of whom had been patients of Rinearson’s optometry practice. Employees were trained to handle everything from making ice cream and waffle cones to packing pints and decorating cakes and other confections. The idea was straightforward: give people a real job, teach them skills and allow them to become more independent.From one ice-cream shop to two businessesJake’s Ice Cream, located in the Barcroft Plaza Shopping Center in Lincolnia, now has 24 employees. The business was followed by Jake’s Gourmet Popcorn, which opened three years ago at Seven Corners Shopping Center. Eleven people work there, bringing the combined workforce of the two businesses to 35. For Rinearson, however, the number of employees is only part of the story. Many of her workers stay for years and often recommend the jobs to friends. The result, she said, is unusual for a small business: there is a waiting list of prospective employees.The job is meant to lead somewhereRinearson does not view the stores simply as places where employees can spend their working lives. The skills they learn, from serving customers and handling food to working as part of a team and completing workplace responsibilities, can potentially help them pursue other employment opportunities.Fairfax County’s proclamation similarly highlighted the businesses for strengthening employees’ independence, developing workplace skills and helping create a more inclusive community. The approach is also consistent with what Rinearson has said about the shop in earlier interviews. In 2022, she described the business as a place where employees could receive meaningful, year-round work rather than simply seasonal employment.A national award brings wider attentionIn July 2026, PBATS selected Jake’s Gourmet Popcorn and Jake’s Ice Cream as its Washington, DC-area recipient of the Ability Transcends Challenges Award. The annual programme recognises businesses committed to disability inclusion and employment. In 2026, PBATS expanded the awards to include one organisation in each of the 30 MLB cities, with the National Down Syndrome Society as a partner and support from the US Department of Labor’s Office of Disability Employment Policy.PBATS president Nick Kenney said the programme is built around the idea that opportunity, support and inclusion should extend beyond sport and into communities and workplaces. For Rinearson, that philosophy has played out behind an ice-cream counter and inside a popcorn shop. What began as a way to make sure people like her nephew had somewhere to work has become a small local employment ecosystem, one where the unusual problem is no longer finding people who want the jobs, but having more people waiting for a chance to get one.You use AI every day. articles.body: Target is joining the Thanksgiving meal-deal race with a pitch that pairs budget-friendly staples with fresh twists on holiday favorites. articles.title: G20 foreign ministers scrap ‘family photo’ as Lavrov crashes party
articles.summary: The U.S. hosts of the Group of 20 (G20) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting opted to skip the traditional “family photo” Friday after several top diplomats objected to being photographed with a Russian official. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s presence at the two-day event in Atlanta raised tensions within the group because of his country’s ongoing military…
articles.body:
The U.S. hosts of the Group of 20 (G20) Foreign Ministers’ Meeting opted to skip the traditional “family photo” Friday after several top diplomats objected to being photographed with a Russian official.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s presence at the two-day event in Atlanta raised tensions within the group because of his country’s ongoing military offensive in Ukraine, which has waged on for almost five years.

A U.S. official confirmed to The Hill that event hosts opted to skip the ceremonial photo after it became apparent some diplomats were unwilling to participate. The official said the move served to avoid a potential diplomatic distraction and keep the focus trained on the meeting’s priorities.

“There is no ‘business as usual’ with Russia,” German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul told reporters in Atlanta, according to Bloomberg . “We need to discuss these controversies here at the table, which is why this conversation is important. But we must also avoid sending the wrong visual signals.”

At a September G20 gathering in Asheville, N.C., Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov was omitted from a group picture after several members and allies said they would not participate if he was involved.

The cancellation of the traditional photo at the Atlanta meeting comes amid tensions within the G20 over the Trump administration’s recent diesel deal with Russia and decision to halt the implementation of recently passed Russian sanctions — outlined under a legislative package dedicated to the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.).

The two-day gathering in Atlanta comes ahead of the group’s summit with foreign leaders at Trump National Doral Golf Club in Miami. The president has extended an invite to Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend the gathering.

On Friday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio opened the meeting of foreign ministers with a warning that the world faces a “moment of choosing” against a backdrop of mounting economic and geopolitical tensions.

“As diplomats, as political leaders, we have a vital role to play,” Rubio told the group.

“We are tasked, on behalf of the nations that we serve, to work together with one another to coordinate responses to emerging crises and to protect our shared interests,” he continued. “By translating our shared interest into practical cooperation and real action, we can reinforce global stability, and more importantly, we can deliver meaningful results for our citizens.”

articles.title: Swiss supreme court upholds Liberian ex-rebel commander’s 20-year sentence
articles.summary: Alieu Kosiah killed civilians and unarmed soldiers, and ordered lootings and other crimes against humanity.
articles.body:
Switzerland’s supreme court upheld a 20-year jail sentence for former Liberian rebel commander Alieu Kosiah on Friday, but overturned a conviction for crimes against humanity.

In 2021, Switzerland’s Federal Criminal Court found Kosiah, now 51, guilty of multiple atrocities committed during the first of Liberia’s back-to-back civil wars, in which about 250,000 people died between 1989 and 2003.

In 2023, the court’s appeals chamber upheld his 20-year sentence for war crimes and, for the first time in Swiss history, also made a new ruling that Kosiah was guilty of crimes against humanity.

The Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland was asked to review the case, and its verdict, dated September 28, was published on Friday.

The court “rejected the appeal filed by a high-ranking Liberian military official challenging his conviction for violations of the laws of war committed between 1993 and 1995 during the first Liberian civil war”, it said in a statement.

“However, the court has acquitted the individual of the charge of crimes against humanity, based on a strict application of the principle of non-retroactivity.”

Switzerland recognises the principle of universal jurisdiction, which allows it to prosecute individuals suspected of international crimes, regardless of where those crimes were committed.

The court said the offence of crimes against humanity – introduced into Swiss law in 2011 – could not be applied to acts committed before then.

Kosiah’s conviction for violating the law of war was upheld, as was the maximum 20-year custodial sentence imposed.

“The decision makes final the first war crimes conviction ever handed down by a Swiss civilian court, and the first conviction anywhere of a Liberian for war crimes committed during the country’s civil wars,” said the Swiss organisation Civitas Maxima, which works to bring perpetrators of international crimes to justice.

Kosiah settled in Switzerland in the late 1990s and was arrested in 2014.

“Today the survivors of Alieu Kosiah’s crimes have final justice,” said Civitas Maxima director Alain Werner, who represents victims in the case.

“We are, however, deeply disappointed by the acquittal on crimes against humanity. What happened in Lofa between 1993 and 1995 is the very definition of a crime against humanity.”

Like war crimes, crimes against humanity refer to atrocities, including murder, torture and rape. However, instead of isolated or sporadic events, the charge is used for incidents carried out in a widespread or systematic way.

In the 2021 verdict, Kosiah was found guilty of a slew of war crimes committed as commander of the United Liberation Movement of Liberia for Democracy rebel group.

He ordered or participated in the killing of 17 civilians and two unarmed soldiers, as well as rape and the deployment of a child soldier, the court ruled.

He had also ordered looting and repeatedly ordered, or had himself inflicted, cruel and humiliating treatment of civilians and mishandled corpses, according to the verdict.

articles.title: Treasury Department says Iran’s economy cratering, inflation at 90 percent
articles.summary: The U.S.’s economic isolation campaign against Iran is “decimating” the country’s economy, according to a Treasury Department report released Friday. The Trump administration launched its sweeping economic pressure campaign, dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, at the end of August. During a Wednesday appearance on CNBC, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the effort has been “very successful.”…
articles.body:
The U.S.’s economic isolation campaign against Iran is “decimating” the country’s economy , according to a Treasury Department report released Friday.

The Trump administration launched its sweeping economic pressure campaign , dubbed Operation Economic Outcast, at the end of August. During a Wednesday appearance on CNBC, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the effort has been “very successful.”

The Treasury Department report found that Iran’s headline inflation, which measures the overall increase in prices across all goods and services in an economy, reached 90 percent in September after the operation was announced.

Before the U.S. and Israel set off the conflict with joint strikes on Tehran at the end of February, headline inflation in Iran was sitting at around 70 percent. Core inflation, which excludes volatile items like food and energy, was just above 70 percent in September.

“As the rial loses value and Iran’s access to international markets narrows, inflation is placing additional pressure on Iran’s already strained economy,” the report stated. “Rising prices are eroding purchasing power and increasing the cost of basic goods, while making it more expensive for Iran to obtain goods and inputs from abroad.”

The unofficial rial exchange rate hit 2,687,000 Iranian rials per U.S. dollar in October, according to the Treasury Department.

The report also indicated that Tehran’s oil supplies have taken a hit amid U.S. sanctions and a months-long U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil trading corridor.

The department said Iran has not loaded any oil onto vessels since Aug. 25, the day after Bessent announced Operation Economic Outcast. Iran is left with “nothing” after it sold its oil that was stranded at sea, according to the Treasury Department report.

Iran’s aviation sector and formal financial sector have also been mired by the U.S.’s efforts to crush the country’s economy. The Treasury Department said it is also targeting “alternative channels” Iran has sought out to move money and skirt restrictions.

“By identifying and disrupting cryptocurrency exchanges, wallets, financial facilitators, and other digital-asset infrastructure used to circumvent sanctions, Treasury is making it increasingly difficult for the regime to replace traditional financial channels with new ones,” the report stated.

Critics of the Trump administration’s military and economic campaigns against Iran have pointed to domestic fiscal impacts, including the rising cost of fuel. The average price of a standard gallon of gas in the U.S. was up to $4.20 Friday afternoon, around a 38 percent increase from a year ago, according to AAA .

articles.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
articles.summary: The American-made interceptors are the only effective weapon for downing Russia's ballistic missiles.
articles.body:
The US has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, a critically-needed munition for defence against escalating Russian aerial attacks, after Kyiv said deliveries had been delayed in recent months.

The US State Department said the advanced PAC-3 interceptor missiles would cost $2.1bn (£1.6bn) and would be "funded entirely" by Kyiv's allies in Europe and Canada.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly urged the US to speed up deliveries of its Patriots - the only effective weapon in downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles.

The latest move comes just days after a row between Zelensky and Donald Trump, with the US president saying it was time for Ukraine to get a new leader to try to end the war with Russia.

In Friday's statement, the State Department said "this proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe".

It said "Ukraine will pay for this purchase with donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union's Ukraine Support Loan".

The statement said the "principal contractor" would be American company Lockheed Martin, adding that "no US funds are involved in this sale".

Zelensky said earlier this week that his country had been waiting almost a month for the US to sign off on critical missile supplies.

And in a Telegram post late on Friday, the Ukrainian president reported that earlier in the day Russian ballistic missiles had struck two of the country's regions.

"They continue to carry out terrorist strikes against our cities," he said.

Zelensky has recently admitted that Ukraine was running critically low on Patriots, as Russia was intensifying its attacks on key energy infrastructure ahead of winter.

Kyiv desperately needs the interceptors but there is a global shortage of the munitions due to their use by the US in its war against Iran.

It is not clear what the production schedule will be for the Patriots - but it is understood the order is for new builds rather than existing missiles, meaning there is unlikely to be any kind of rapid delivery to Ukraine.

Patriots also have lengthy production times, with only 600 missiles produced per year according to the US Department of Defence.

In July, Trump said Washington had "not agreed" to license Ukraine to produce Patriots - three weeks after offering the country such a right.

articles.title: George and Amal Clooney’s foundation reports free legal services for over 9,000 women and children, with mobile clinics taking help to communities affected by child marriage and violence
articles.summary: For women and girls facing child marriage, domestic abuse or discrimination, getting legal help can be difficult when lawyers are expensive or courts are
articles.body: For women and girls facing child marriage, domestic abuse or discrimination, getting legal help can be difficult when lawyers are expensive or courts are far away. The Clooney Foundation for Justice is working to address these barriers through free legal assistance, community-based clinics and legal advocacy. Co-founded by actor George Clooney and human rights lawyer Amal Clooney, the organisation says its work has helped thousands of women and children access legal services and defend their rights.According to the foundation's official Our Impact page, more than 9,000 women and children have received free legal services, while its broader work includes over 10,000 hours of free legal aid in defence of women's rights and free speech. Its Waging Justice for Women programme works with local organisations to reach marginalised communities, including remote areas affected by child marriage and gender-based violence. The foundation also supports women lawyers through fellowships designed to strengthen legal representation and advocacy across Africa.Mobile legal clinics reach women in remote communitiesOne of the foundation's key initiatives is its mobile legal aid programme, which brings legal advice and support closer to women and girls who might otherwise struggle to access the justice system. Through its Waging Justice for Women programme, the foundation partnered with the Women Lawyers Association (WLA) in Malawi to establish mobile clinics in 12 communities identified as child marriage hotspots. According to its impact report, these clinics advised more than 4,000 women and girls on issues including gender-based violence, protective orders and financial independence for women and their children.The clinics are designed to address practical barriers to legal support. Women facing abuse or discrimination may not know their legal rights, have the money to hire a lawyer or be able to travel to a legal aid centre. By working with local women's organisations and lawyers, the programme offers a more accessible way to seek advice and representation. The foundation also reports that its technical and substantive support helped the Women Lawyers Association of Malawi reach almost 7,000 people in 2024 through legal information, advice and representation. This figure covers the association's broader legal services and should be distinguished from the foundation's separate figure for women and girls advised through the 12 mobile clinics.Tackling child marriage and gender-based violenceThe foundation's women's rights work extends beyond individual legal cases. Its Waging Justice for Women programme, launched in 2022, combines legal representation, strategic litigation and public advocacy to challenge discriminatory laws and improve access to justice. Child marriage is one of its central areas of focus. The foundation works with local partners to provide legal support to girls and women affected by the practice, while also advocating for changes to laws and policies that permit or fail to prevent it.The organisation has also highlighted the connection between gender-based violence and barriers to accountability. Survivors may encounter stigma, inadequate legal protection or difficulties reporting abuse. Through its partners, the foundation seeks to help survivors obtain legal assistance while challenging practices that prevent women from pursuing justice. Its work includes support for legal action in South Africa concerning laws that can silence survivors of sexual violence and their supporters. The foundation says these efforts are intended to strengthen accountability and make it easier for victims to seek redress.Fellowships prepare the next generation of women lawyersAnother part of the initiative focuses on building the capacity of women lawyers who can represent women and children in their own communities. The foundation's fellowship programme provides placements, training and mentoring for early-career African women lawyers. Fellows work with legal aid organisations, universities, human rights groups and government prosecution services, gaining practical experience in legal research, client support, court representation and advocacy. According to the foundation's fellowship page, since the programme began in 2023, its fellows have worked on more than 500 cases concerning women's and children's rights and supported over 2,000 women and children through legal assistance, advocacy and legal education. Their work has addressed issues including gender-based violence, reproductive rights and child marriage.From August 2026, the Waging Justice for Women Fellowship Programme was renamed the CFJ Fellowship Programme. The foundation says its recruitment, eligibility requirements and application processes remain unchanged. The initiative is intended to build a network of legal professionals who can continue working on women's rights after their placements end. Fellows receive mentoring and training and can join an alumni network for continued professional support.Legal advocacy extends beyond individual casesThe foundation's wider impact includes efforts to change laws and policies through court cases and advocacy. In Tanzania, the foundation supported legal action that contributed to the reversal of a policy excluding married and pregnant girls from school. In El Salvador, the foundation reports that its intervention in a case involving the prosecution of women following miscarriages contributed to a compensation order of $200,000 and legal reforms.Together, these initiatives illustrate the different ways the Clooney Foundation for Justice approaches access to justice: providing immediate legal assistance, supporting local organisations, training lawyers and challenging discriminatory rules. Its reported figure of more than 9,000 women and children receiving free legal services reflects the scale of that work, while the mobile clinics demonstrate how legal support can reach communities that might otherwise remain underserved.You use AI every day. articles.title: Polish president turns plane around after 'coup' at nation’s top court
articles.summary: Tensions between Poland’s president and prime minister intensified as demonstrators rally outside the country’s top court.
articles.body: While en route to Senegal, Poland’s President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around and returned home after police entered Poland's top court, the Constitutional Tribunal, and the tribunal’s president was suspended."At such a moment, the President must be in Poland," Nawrocki posted on X. "I'm interrupting my flight to Senegal. I'm returning."Police say they secured the Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered to demonstrate against what they called the wrongful suspension of the top court’s president by the current pro-European government. Police said there were also dangerous objects thrown at officers outside the building. Some protesters outside the court were seen praying, while others held posters reading "Tusk — a symbol of anti-Polish sentiment," "Down with the commies and Tusk’s regime," and "Stop destroying the state."Poland’s top judicial bodies, including the Constitutional Tribunal, have been a major bone of contention between the current pro-European government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, and the main opposition party, national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which ruled the country from 2015 to 2023. Critics accuse the PiS of imposing political control over key judicial institutions, with some reforms having led the EU to impose fines on Poland. NATO ALLY PUSHES ‘FORT TRUMP’ US MILITARY BASE AS RUSSIAN HELICOPTER PENETRATES AIRSPACENawrocki, an ally of the PiS ​party, refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament earlier this year. Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Święczkowski, ⁠who was appointed by the PiS government after also serving as a deputy justice minister, declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to assume their duties. According to the tribunal’s website, Święczkowski was suspended Friday. "Restoring the rule of law is our duty," said Tusk, who returned to power in 2023 with a promise to restore the judiciary’s independence. He posted to X, "After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way." Since taking power, Tusk’s pro-European government’s efforts have been vetoed by two successive presidents aligned with PiS, including Nawrocki. HUNGARY AND POLAND DEFEND TOUGH MIGRATION POLICIES AS FRANCE REELS FROM VIOLENT UNRESTFormer Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki, a former PiS member whose Rozwój Plus coalition is positioning itself as an alternative to Tusk's government ahead of next November’s parliamentary elections, also took to X to denounce "the forceful takeover of the Constitutional Tribunal." "Justice cannot be achieved through violence," Morawiecki said, adding that "Tusk will stop at nothing to cling to power… We do not consent to Belarusian methods in Poland!" "It’s true: a coup d’état is underway," former PiS Justice Minister Zbigniew Ziobro wrote on X. "If someone were to forcibly break into the Prime Minister’s Office and take it over, we would all know what to call it… This is a blatant, criminal attack on the constitutional order… That is why I call for resistance that will be loud, firm, solidary and fearless." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP"A judge whose oath was never accepted by the President Nawrocki has declared herself head of the Constitutional Tribunal and suspended its leadership, while police secured the building," added Morawiecki. "This is not how the rule of law is restored. The tribunal's crisis is real, but replacing one disputed set of rules with a more radical one only invites the next government to do the same." U.S. Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose posted a statement on social media that read in part: "The events unfolding tonight at Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal are very serious indeed. We appear to be witnessing an unprecedented confrontation over the government’s use of state power and the independence and authority of a constitutional institution. Both sides offer sharply different accounts of what happened and why. Whatever the facts ultimately establish, thousands gathering outside the Tribunal make an already dangerous situation more combustible. The last thing Poland needs is a confrontation that spirals into something far worse. America is on Poland’s side. It is not our place to judge or interfere in its internal affairs. Our concern is for the stability, security, and democratic future of a country we are proud to call our friend and ally."The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Love, luck and magic: Why are young people turning to online witches?
articles.summary: One online retailer has reported a sharp rise in the amount of people buying spells to help with luck.
articles.body:
Love or luck, take your pick. All yours with a simple click.

Or at least that's the promise being made by so-called "Etsy witches", who claim to cast spells for everything from good fortune to good weather.

And it seems there's a growing appetite for a little magic. Online retailer Etsy says searches for weather spells and witches have significantly increased this year.

But what are people hoping to get from these online witches, and why are young people turning to them for a helping hand?

For one 'Etsy witch', there's certainly no shortage of people looking for some extra luck.

Ellecia Cahill, from Erskine, describes herself as a "mystic" and has clocked up more than 2,000 sales online from readings and channelled letters - messages which claim to be from loved ones - as well as selling crystals and amulets.

And while you might expect love spells to top the shopping list, she says there's something else her customers are particularly keen on.

Abundance spells - in other words, a little help attracting money, success and opportunities.

She claims one customer - a tech investor from the wealthy Mediterranean principality of Monaco - had seen a "significant increase" in his net worth since he bought an abundance talisman.

A scroll through similar online retailers reveals a spell for every occasion, including spells promising to keep the rain away on your wedding day or to help you get tickets to a sold-out concert.

A spokesperson for Etsy told BBC Scotland they have seen "growing interest" in "magical touches" for occasions like weddings.

They said searches for spells for people trying to ensure sunshine on their big day have grown by 206% while general searches for wedding related-spells and witches are up 105%.

Whether they can actually deliver is another question entirely - in fact, Etsy rules say spells must be marketed as for entertainment purposes only.

For Cahill, it's not all about doing business.

The 24-year-old says that young people - though they are very used to thinking logically - are looking to believe in something magical.

She says that a lot of younger people feel lonely, and she wants to be a "safe space" for people, and to give them comfort.

"As humans we need to believe in something that is bigger than ourselves," she said. "Curiosity is natural.

"I think a lot of the time people know the answer they want, but are just looking for a bit of reassurance.

"Even if magic isn't real, if it helps someone feel more confident what is the harm?"

Actress Laura Blair, from Glasgow, bought a spell to help her with a specific job goal.

The 29-year-old told BBC Scotland: "I paid for a job spell, and they then allocated me to a witch. I had to send them my full names and more specifics and then she sent me a video of her doing the spell."

While the purchase didn't work out exactly as she'd hoped, she has noticed a positive impact on her acting career generally.

"Since I cast the spells I've had multiple acting roles, its actually the busiest I've ever been in my career," she said.

Another user, Chloe, also from Glasgow, wasn't so happy with her results.

"It was a waste of time and money. What I asked for didn't happen but it is a funny story, I suppose," the 22-year-old said.

"I had just gone through a break-up and wanted my ex back - but in hindsight maybe it is just as well it didn't work."

Researcher Alexandria Arthur-Hastie is a sociologist of religion at Leeds Beckett University. She believes the rise of online witches is part of a broader shift away from traditional religion and towards more "personalised forms of spirituality".

Hastie said it was unsurprising that witchcraft had expanded online, just like other aspects of modern life which have moved onto digital platforms.

"It's really just the latest step in the commodification of spirituality," she told BBC Scotland.

She said shows likes Sabrina the Teenage Witch and Charmed brought magic into the mainstream and these days, people can discover witchcraft through social media.

But the academic says there's something deeper behind the appeal.

For some young people, she said turning to witchcraft can be a way of finding support when life feels uncertain - be it relationships, careers or worries about the future.

"People go online, they're looking for solutions to these life problems, they're looking for a balm to soothe, really," she said.

Hastie said many contemporary witches see themselves not as mystical figures but as healers, focused on helping themselves, others and wider society.

"They really see it almost as a caring profession, something akin to maybe counselling," she said.

articles.title: Democrats weigh Israel election results amid lingering uncertainty
articles.summary: The results of Israel’s elections this week have left Democrats on Capitol Hill with a mixed bag of emotions.
